work.title: Passion of Jonah and Barachisius (29 March)

paragraphs.text: March 29. The martyrdom of Saint Jonah and Barachisius and his companions. In the eighteenth year of Shapur, king of Persia, a persecution arose against the churches of Christ and those who worshiped God Almighty.

King Shapur ordered the impious Magi to set fire to the holy Christian churches. He ordered that any Christians found should be arrested and forced to offer sacrifices and obey the priests. Those who obeyed and offered sacrifices were to be raised to high ranks and honors, but those who refused to obey were to be subjected to bitter and various tortures. At that time of persecution, there were in the land of Persia, in a certain village called Iasa, two brothers named Barachisius and Jonah, righteous men, full of faith and keeping the Lord’s commandments with reverence. When these two saints heard of the persecution of Christians, they left their home and went to the place where the impious Magi were cruelly torturing Christians. When they reached the village of Vardachov, they approached the prison where all the Christians were confined. They fell down before the prison guard and begged him to let them enter the prison. When they entered, they found nine Christian men imprisoned there. Seeing them in great distress, they greeted them with a kiss and began to encourage them, saying, “Let us fear nothing, brothers and fathers, but let us suffer in the name of the Crucified One

for a single hour, so that we may receive eternal life, just as our fathers, the sufferers for Christ and martyrs, received it.” Likewise, when those martyrs saw Saints Jonah and Barachisius, they became more eager because of their arrival. The two saints also gave much other instruction, and, as though anointing one another with grace-filled oil to endure torture and complete their martyrdom, they strengthened one another. The names of the holy martyrs confined in the prison are these: Zanithas, Lazarus, Maruthas, Narses, Elijah, Maris, Abibus, Simboethes, and Sabbas. These men were then tortured and endured many afflictions, and they died in the struggle of martyrdom, having finished their race well, and with martyrial and imperishable [?] They crowned themselves with an unfading crown. And when those saints had been tortured, and had flown up to heaven and been admitted into the company of angels, afterward some of the Magi accused the saints Jonah and Barachisius before the three chief Magi, Masdrath, Sirath, and Maarnisius, who were judging the saints, saying, “These two neither offer sacrifices nor obey the king’s command, nor are they willing to worship fire or the sun

or water.” Besides this, they also reviled them, saying that those nine men [?] had not obeyed the emperor’s command, having been turned away by these two. Then the chief priests, filled with great rage, ordered the two to be brought in. When they had been brought in and stood before the chief Magi, the Magi said to them, “We adjure you by our invincible King Shapur: answer us without lying about what we ask you. Do you carry out the emperor’s will and obey his command, and worship the sun and fire and water, according to the law and commandment of our emperor, or not?” The saints Jonah and Barachisius answered them, saying, “Let us speak, and listen as princes and judges of the king of Persia, for whom you have been chosen, and as just judges. For this reason he chose you and entrusted all his judgment into your hands, so that you might judge justly and not act unjustly. Now then, you illustrious judges, you should not fear an earthly emperor, but the one who gave you wisdom and understanding, who has power over heaven and earth and every breathing creature, who set boundaries and appointed times, and gives

wisdom [?], will give you wisdom, so that according to your wisdom [?] you may judge justly those who are like you in the flesh [?]. We therefore adjure you by the true faith: tell us which God we ought to renounce—the heavenly or the earthly, the eternal or the short-lived? We believe in God, who made heaven and earth, and we do not believe in a mortal man. We cannot believe in a man who lives a little while, dies, and is buried just as we are.” When the Magi heard this from them, they became very angry and ordered thorny rods, with the thorns unstripped, to be brought for the torture of the saints Jonah and Barachisius. Having separated them from one another, so that neither of the two would hear his companion's interrogation and gain strength to suffer for Christ. Then Masrath, Siroth, and Marnisius, the three chief Magi, took their seats to interrogate the two saints, and angrily ordered that Saint Jonah alone be brought in. When Jonah had been brought in, the Magi said to him, “What do you think? Will you honor and worship the sun, fire, and water, and carry out the king's command? Otherwise, we will inflict harsh and exceedingly cruel tortures on you. Do not think

to yourself that we want you to suffer any harm. We wish you no harm at all, unless you yourself wish to bring harm upon yourself.” The blessed Jonah answered them, “I have no need of this life, for the sake of life in Christ. For this life passes away and never lasts. Therefore I will never deny my Lord Jesus Christ, who lives forever, for he is the hope of all Christians. And none of those who believe in him will be put to shame. For he promised us, saying, ‘Truly, truly, I tell you: whoever denies me before others, I too will deny him before my Father in heaven and before the holy angels.’ For he will come on the clouds of heaven in the glory of his Father and of the holy angels and archangels. And everything is already prepared for each person to be repaid according to his deeds. Now that you have heard this, carry out quickly the command you have been given concerning what to do to me. Do not think that I will abandon the Lord's house, since he appointed us to serve in his holy house. And he said to us, ‘You are the light of the world,’ and again, ‘You are the salt of the earth. If the salt loses its flavor, how

will it become salty again?’ Therefore, if we obey the king's command, as you say, and carry out his orders, then we will not be the only ones to deny our Lord: our denial will cause everyone to do so.” When the chief Magi heard this from the two of them, they became exceedingly angry and ordered him to be bound according to Persian custom, and they thrust a rod between his arms and thighs. The saint was sitting on the ground. As he sat there, they tortured him with knotty rods. They tortured him until his ribs were laid bare. But while he was being tortured, he made no reply at all. But he glorified God, saying: “Glory to you, God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Lead us out of this world, since you have deemed us worthy to be brought to your holy faith. And now, Lord, give us endurance, so that we may carry out and complete everything your Holy Spirit has commanded us. And grant that I may please you by ending my life as a martyr. For this is what I await every day.” And having said this, Saint Jonah said in a loud voice to the magi: “I withdraw from your prince and from all your companions, who are Satan’s angels, and I reject them all. And I renounce the sun, the moon, the stars, fire, and water, which you regard as

gods. I have nothing to do with them, and I will not worship them at all. Instead, I believe in the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, in the most pure Trinity, who saves the whole world and who also created your gods, which you are forcing me to worship.” Hearing this, the chief magi ordered them to tie a rope around his foot and drag him outside into the frost, and to leave him on the ice all night, for it was winter, and to watch him to see what he would do to the ice. They did so and watched him with great fear, leaving him there until daybreak. Then the lawless men again sat on their judgment seat and ordered the servants to bring Saint Barachisius before them. When the saint had entered and stood before the tribunal, the magi said to him: “What are you thinking, Barachisius? Will you offer sacrifice and worship the sun, fire, and water, just as your brother Jonah obeyed and worshiped them? Or will you receive wounds on your body?” Saint Barachisius answered them: “Just as Jonah worshiped the one he worshiped, so I too will worship him all the more, glorify him, and exalt him. You have spoken a lie about Jonah. But the truth will not allow him to do that. For who could blind the understanding of his heart, so that he would worship a created thing that serves human beings, and abandon the one who created

him? For if the created thing were worthy of honor, it would receive glorious service from human beings and would not serve us like a slave. For now we see that both rich and poor, both evil and good, receive service from it. Your fire is a slave to human beings, who are greater than it, and [?] the one who created it and ordained it this way for us. For it is wrong to force us to bow down in worship to this world (God, for our use, gave this fire to us human beings), and to abandon God, who made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them. Rather, it is fitting that praise, worship, and honor be received from kings, princes, commanders, and every breathing creature by him who made the heights and the depths, whose deep thoughts no one can fathom, and upon the height of whose glory no one is able to gaze, whom all of us sons of men need. For he is the one who feeds the whole inhabited world, and he has prepared everything by his wisdom. This is what he requires of us: that all of us sons of men should know the name of our Lord, and not be deceived by futile deeds and falsehoods. For he said, “Do not make shrines for yourselves, and do not bow down to the works of your hands or to any other created thing, because I

am the Lord your God, who exists from the beginning and remains to the end, and there is no other god besides me. I will not give my glory to another, nor my favor to carved images, nor will I give my honor to shrines. I put to death and bring to life, and there is no one who will escape my hand.” Then the chief Magi grew angry when they heard these words from him. They began to marvel at them and their endurance, and said, “Let us not question him now, so that none of those who honor and worship the sun, fire, and water will hear such words from him and likewise renounce them and turn away from sacrifices. Instead, let us hear them at night, so that no one learns what the two of them say or what we do.” And so it happened. Then they rose from the judgment seat without passing judgment. When they sat down at night, and there was deep silence, they ordered Saint Barachisius to be brought in. When he had been brought in, and there was deep silence, they listened to him. After the Magi had questioned him at length, and the saint had overcome them through God's wisdom, the lawless men grew angry and ordered copper slabs to be brought. They heated them until they were hotter than fire and placed them under both his armpits.

And the Magi said to him, “By the crown of Shapur, king of Persia,” For if you shake even a single [?] out of your bosom and it falls to the ground, then know that I now know for certain that he has renounced his God. Saint Barachisius answered them, saying, “Servants of Satan and sinful rulers! As surely as my God brings salvation, and Satan your father faces destruction, I will not fear your god and throw even one of the [?] to the ground. Instead, for the sake of my Christ’s name, I will hold on to them. And now I adjure you by the living God: if you have other cruel tortures besides this torture, inflict them on us. For who goes out to battle without committing himself wholeheartedly to death, so that he may receive great glory and many gifts from the emperor, and high rank?” When Saint Barachisius had said this, the magi became furious and ordered lead to be brought, melted, and poured over his eyes, and poured into his nostrils, his mouth, and his ears, so that he could neither hear nor speak. Then they commanded the servants, saying, “Take him and lead him into prison, tie him by one leg, and hang him there.” And they did so. After they had said this, the impious magi again ordered the blessed Jonah to be brought to them. When he came,

the magi said to him: to bring the blessed Jonah to them. When he came, the magi said to him, “What is it, Jonah? How does your flesh look to you? And how did you endure that whole night standing on the ice and in the bitter cold?” The blessed Jonah answered them and said, “Know, judges and kings, that my God, whom my soul has chosen—ever since my father begot me, as far as I remember and know— has never given me such a good night. I do not remember, since I have been among human beings and learned what sensation is, such a restful night passing over me. For relief came to me from the holy tree on which my Lord Jesus Christ was crucified.” When Saint Jonah had said this, the magi answered him and said, “Your brother Barachisius has renounced your God, yet you still remain faithful to him.” Saint Jonah answered them, saying, “I too know that he has renounced the devil and all his angels, and has offered himself wholly to Christ the Lord.” The magi said to him, “Do not bring your soul to a miserable end. It is better for you to renounce your God.” Jonah answered them, “You blind fools! You yourselves say, ‘We are wise, and through our wisdom we shall discover [?].’

Can a man who has wheat lying in his granary and keeps it there, when rain, clouds, and thunder and lightning come, refrain from taking some wheat into his hand and sowing it in the Lord’s name? After sowing, he waits for the harvest to come and fill his threshing floor from that little amount he sowed, because of the hope he had in Christ. But if he neglects the wheat, leaving it lying in the granary, and does not sow any of it, then the wheat will run short, for it cannot increase. We can see the same thing among us human beings. If someone loses his soul for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, then, when he wills to renew the children of men— those who hope in him and do his will— that person will be renewed by that light of his which does not pass away or ever perish. And those who have disregarded his commandments he will throw into unquenchable fire.” When the magi heard this, they were speechless for a long time, marveling at his words. Finally they answered him, “Do not deceive yourself, Jonah, and listen to [?].” The blessed Jonah answered them, “You were right to say that [?] deceive, but those that come from you pagans. Nothing else deceives people except the life of this world.

But whoever tastes the Lord’s sufferings is never deceived. For just as a certain rich man, having prepared a great feast for his guests and sent for those he had invited, sees the invited guests set out, each from his own house, knowing for certain that they are going to a celebration and eagerly coming to the feast, they enter for the meal, sit down at the table, and taste the wine. If it is good, they drink it with pleasure and become merry, and because of their drunkenness they cannot go home, since they have drunk a great deal, delighting themselves with wine, until their own people come and take hold of them and bring them to their homes. When they rise in the morning, once the wine has worn off, they rejoice greatly that they have been lying at home among their own people. So too the servants of Christ, when they see that the judges are summoning them to the judgment seat, know that they are going to hardship and suffering. When they go and become drunk with suffering and with the love of Christ, then they no longer remember their homes, their children, or their possessions, nor can they acquire gold or silver or anything else in this world, but they scorn both emperor and prince, awaiting only the one great King, Christ, whose soldiers we are, who endures from generation to generation,

whose kingdom does not pass away but endures forever. When Saint Jonah had said this, the magi ordered his fingers and toes to be cut off, both those on his hands and those on his feet. They threw them before Saint Jonah, and the magi said to him, “See how we have scattered your fingers and toes on the ground. Wait, then, until harvest time comes, and you will have many fingers and toes.” Saint Jonah answered, “I have no need of many hands. But there is God, who created me, who will restore me again through his renewal, which he intends to bring about for us.” When the magi heard this from him, they were filled with rage and ordered pitch to be boiled in a cauldron. They ordered the servants to flay his entire head all around, wherever there was hair, and also to cut out his tongue. They did so. Then the magi gave an order, and they threw the skin of his head and his tongue into the cauldron of pitch before his eyes. Then they threw the saint himself into the cauldron of pitch. When the saint had been thrown in, the cauldron and all the pitch immediately spilled out, and it did not touch him or harm him in any way at all. When the impious magi saw the miracle that had taken place, they marveled

and were astonished that such torture had not harmed him at all. They ordered a press to be brought, and ordered him to be put into it and squeezed and twisted severely. The servants did so, and all his bones were broken. Then they crushed him in two. When he had been crushed, the magi ordered his body to be thrown into a deep pit and guarded securely. And so it was done. After Saint Jonah had thus met his end, they ordered Saint Barachisius to be brought in again. When he had been brought in, the magi said to him, “Spare your limbs, Barachisius, and do not choose to condemn yourself to an untimely death.” Saint Barachisius answered them, “I am not the one who created myself.” “Nor am I destroying myself. Rather, it is the Lord who made me, and he will renew me by his power. And he will deliver me and keep me blameless, safe from your hands and from the hands of your disgraced emperor, who does not know the God who made him, but the will and commands of that devil he strives to carry out.” When Saint Barachisius had said this, the magi said, “Are we ourselves the ones insulting and reviling Emperor Shapur? These men, trusting in their own deception, have no regard for anyone.” When they had said this to them

and were filled with great rage, all their faces changed because of the blessed Barachisius. They ordered him to be dragged over thorns. Then they ordered reeds to be brought, split in two, and laid against his flesh. They were to be bound with a rope and tightened until the reeds sank into his flesh. Then they ordered the reeds to be pulled out of him, so that his flesh would be torn away along with the reeds. The servants did so and pulled out the reeds together with his flesh. Then the impious magi gave an order, and they put him into the [?] where they had also put Saint Jonah, and there they broke all his bones. Then they gave orders to the servants, who brought burning pitch and poured it into his mouth. And so Saint Barachisius gave up his soul. Thus he suffered along with all the saints. When a certain devout man named Audisoth heard that the saints had died— Jonah and Barachisius—he came and bought the bodies of the two saints from the guards, paying five hundred and three silver coins. He bought not only the bodies of these two saints alone, but also those of the others who had been tortured before them. This man swore to those who sold the bodies,

“None of your rulers will learn what has happened,” for the man had been a friend of those who had died from the beginning. The saints who died have these names: Jonah, Barachisius, Zanithas, Lazarus, Narses, Elijah, Habib, Maris, Maruthas, Sembethes, and Saba. These eleven sufferers and victorious martyrs labored even to the end for Christ, and for this they were clothed in radiant garments and crowned with an unfading crown by Christ himself. Through the prayers of these saints, may we all receive mercy. The holy martyrs of Christ—nine of them—died on the twenty-seventh day of the month of March. And the other two, on the twenty-ninth of the same month. The account of the saints was written down by a certain man named Isaiah, the son of Adav, who was from the land of Arzanene. He had gone with the magi merely to hear what was happening, and remained after the saints’ martyrdom. Having heard and seen everything with complete certainty, from the very beginning to the end, he took care to write it down with all diligence, for the edification and advancement and salvation and advancement of those who read it, as well as of others who imitate
such grace in Christ. To him be glory and power forever and ever. Amen.
